key_insight: RoboVIP uses Visual Identity Prompting to generate multi-view, temporally consistent synthetic video of robot manipulation scenes, enabling realistic data augmentation that preserves object and robot identity across views and time.
problem_solved: Collecting large-scale, diverse, multi-view manipulation data is expensive and hard to scale; prior image-level or single-view augmentations break cross-view and temporal consistency, limiting policy learning and generalization.
method: Visual Identity Prompting: condition a generative model on reference images (object/robot appearance) so synthesized videos preserve identity across frames and camera views.
Multi-view, temporally consistent video generation: extend diffusion/ video generative techniques to produce synchronized views and coherent motion for whole trajectories.
Augmentation pipeline: splice generated multi-view videos into real manipulation trajectories to expand training datasets for downstream robot policy learning.
impact: Provides a practical way to produce realistic, multi-view manipulation data at scale, improving training diversity and generalization of robot policies without costly real-world collection. This helps researchers and practitioners accelerate robot learning and sim-to-real transfer.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: real capture -> visual identity prompt (reference images) -> multi-view video generator -> augmented training data -> policy training loop
Side-by-side frame grid: synchronized multi-view frames showing identity preservation across cameras and time
Performance chart: bar/line plot comparing policy success rates with and without RoboVIP augmentation
Icons/annotations: camera rig, robot arm, identity badge (for object/robot prompt), and temporal coherence waveform
paper_title: RoboVIP: Multi-View Video Generation with Visual Identity Prompting Augments Robot Manipulation
paper_authors: Boyang Wang, Haoran Zhang, Shujie Zhang, Jinkun Hao, Mingda Jia
